clue.text: Popular tenor interrupting period of success by choice

indicators.note: something that interrupts a stretch breaks into the middle of it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a day, as in 'every dog has its day', is a time of triumph
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A well-liked singer chooses to break into a winning run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is only a link, so 'choice' stands alone as an adjective: choice food is dainty.
explanation.definitionFit: As adjectives both describe something delicate, fine and delicious, like a select morsel.

clue.text: Pickpocket's account of a fool

parts.note: dip is slang for a pickpocket, with the 's kept
tick means credit, an account at a shop

explanation.surface: A thief's tale about an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipstick is informal slang for a stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Disliking work? Manage to stop during period of fasting

indicators.note: a stopper goes into a gap, so these letters are plugged into the middle

parts.note: in can mean during, as in 'in May'
Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter
to do is to manage, as in 'that will do'

explanation.surface: A lazy person asks whether to cope with stopping a fast.
explanation.definitionFit: An indolent person is idle and averse to effort.

clue.text: Make an effort to take in launch of aircraft carrier

indicators.note: to take in something is to enclose it, so the effort word wraps the letter

parts.note: to try is to make an effort

indicators.note: the launch, or start, of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A ship's crew strives to watch a jet's takeoff from a carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aircraft carrier' seems one phrase, but 'aircraft' only gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray is a flat board used for carrying cups and plates, so it is something that carries.

clue.text: Earliest of books doesn't have enough on each significant body of water

indicators.note: the earliest part of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: if something lacks, it is short of what is needed

explanation.surface: A reader complains the first volumes are insufficient for every big lake or ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Sea is the inland sea between south-east Europe and Asia Minor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Sea is a large inland sea, an example of a major expanse of water.

clue.text: Unduly protracted line about disease consuming Haggard

parts.note: on means about, concerning

indicators.note: a thing consuming another swallows it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: gout is a disease of the joints
drawn means haggard, gaunt; the capital disguises it as the author

explanation.surface: A sentence on illness devouring the novelist Rider Haggard goes on far too long.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-drawn-out describes something prolonged to tedious length.

clue.text: Arrived to arrest Unionist draped in old Irish tricolour perhaps as disguise

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so the arrived word holds the rest within

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: the Unionist is draped in the other letters, which surround him

parts.note: the Irish tricolour is an example of a flag

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish Unionist is seized while wrapped in a republican flag as a disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: A Unionist backs Northern Ireland staying in the UK, so being wrapped in the Irish tricolour is an ironic disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Camouflage is concealment by blending in, a form of disguise.

clue.text: Feel pain during kinky sex with American boss

indicators.note: a thing happening during another is inside its time span, so these letters go inside

parts.note: S and M, or SM, is sadomasochism
to ache is to feel pain

explanation.surface: Hurting during bondage with an American chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A sachem is a Native American chief, a leader of a tribe.

clue.text: Return of volunteers to continue after much delay

indicators.note: return means the volunteer letters are read backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve of volunteer soldiers
to last is to continue

explanation.surface: Volunteers come back to keep going after a long wait.
explanation.definitionFit: At last means finally, following a long wait.

clue.text: Adele occasionally accommodated by fruit seller

indicators.note: a guest accommodated by a host is housed inside, so these letters sit within the other piece

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: occasionally means only every other letter of the singer's name is kept

explanation.surface: The singer Adele is now and then put up by a greengrocer.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of ADELE give DL, placed in PEAR. 'fruit seller' looks like one phrase, but 'fruit' is wordplay and 'seller' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedlar is a travelling vendor hawking small goods, so is a kind of seller.

clue.text: Head of Institute finding nothing about glass substitute unfavourable

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, taken alone here
nothing placed about the glass substitute wraps around it

parts.note: nil means nothing
mica, a clear mineral, was used in place of glass in stove windows

explanation.surface: An institute's director judges a glass replacement negatively after finding nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Inimical means hostile or harmful, so conditions that are inimical are adverse.

clue.text: Head of state school admitting Sociology's first to go in outline of government's agenda

parts.note: the Queen was the UK's head of state

indicators.note: a school admitting pupils takes them in, so these letters go inside
the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to go is a coy phrase for to pee

explanation.surface: A monarch lets a sociology pupil into school before setting out the government's plans.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen's Speech is read by the monarch at the opening of Parliament, setting out the government's planned laws.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch's address at Parliament's opening sets out the bills the government plans, a summary of its programme.

clue.text: Count to divulge confidential information

definitions.meaning: to ... is to count, as ... count votes or money
to inform on someone or reveal a secret

explanation.surface: Counting and blabbing secrets are paired.
explanation.definitionFit: Tell has an old sense of reckoning numbers ('all told') and a sense of letting out secrets.

clue.text: Actively pursued question about commercial featuring foxes for instance

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed about the advert, enclosing it
acting actively on these letters stirs them into a new order

parts.note: an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: An advert about foxes is the subject of a question vigorously chased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actively' looks like an adverb on the chase, but it signals the anagram, which forms URUPEDS and wraps the advert just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Foxes walk on four legs, so they are examples of four-footed animals.

clue.text: Very energetic new deputy

indicators.note: making the letters new means putting them in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A tremendously vigorous new second-in-command.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicegerent is one who acts with authority on behalf of a ruler, a stand-in.

clue.text: Regard Labour leader in Lincoln as worthy of respect

parts.note: to regard is to consider

indicators.note: the leader of Labour goes in the president's nickname

parts.note: Abe is the nickname of Abraham Lincoln

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A political commentator rates a Labour leader as admirable as Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is one of the UK's main political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Considerable has an old sense of notable or important, meaning someone of standing and esteem.

clue.text: Demonstrate when party's declaration of intent falls short

indicators.note: falling short means the word stops before its final letter

parts.note: a manifesto is a party's statement of its policies

explanation.surface: Protest because a party's policy document is not enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demonstrate' looks like protesting, but it means to show.
explanation.definitionFit: To manifest is to show clearly or display, as to demonstrate a quality.

clue.text: Weapon left in the possession of Deputy Führer unlikely to cause any damage

indicators.note: something in another's possession is held inside them, so these letters go within

parts.note: Rudolf Hess was Hitler's deputy
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: Hitler's deputy holding a weapon is said to be no threat.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmless means innocuous, posing no danger.

clue.text: Someone favoured hiding deserter in abandoned parsonage

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are hiding the deserter, which sits inside them
abandoned in the sense of wild or uncontrolled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a rat is one who deserts, like rats leaving a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A favoured person keeps a runaway hidden in a derelict vicarage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' looks like a description of the parsonage, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Persona grata is Latin for an acceptable or welcome person, one in favour.

clue.text: Contribute to endless books on Scotland's earliest serfs

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to help is to contribute to
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

indicators.note: the earliest letter of the word is its first

explanation.surface: Pitching in to fund unending Scottish book collections for medieval peasants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotland's earliest' looks like a description of serfs, but it only gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: Helots were the state-owned bondsmen of ancient Sparta, so the word means slaves or serfs.

clue.text: Facing material damage to revenue after United's exit

indicators.note: damage to the letters breaks them up into a new order
an exit means the United letter leaves the word

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: Harm to income after a football club leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exit' takes U out of REVENUE, leaving REVENE, and 'damage to' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Veneer is a thin surface layer laid over cheaper wood, a facing material.

clue.text: Calm and positive after the Spanish exam

indicators.note: the calm and positive pieces come after the Spanish article in the answer

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
even means calm or level
plus means positive

explanation.surface: Someone serene and upbeat having sat a Spanish test.
explanation.walkthrough: The eleven-plus is the British test taken around age eleven to decide entry to grammar school.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleven-plus is a selective school test, an example of an examination.

clue.text: Concern for tree close to stream

parts.note: a fir is a tree

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter, taken alone here

explanation.surface: Worry about a tree standing near a brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' reads as 'near', but it picks the end of 'stream'. 'Concern' is the noun meaning a business.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm is a business, and concern is an old word for a company or enterprise.

clue.text: Pressure to show spirit right away

indicators.note: right away here means the right letter goes away from the word

parts.note: heart means spirit, courage

explanation.surface: Stress makes you display courage immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately', but it removes R.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat in the sense 'the heat is on' means strong pressure or intensity.

clue.text: Astonished by work in French? I'd say

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
en is French for in

indicators.note: say means the words are spoken out loud, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: the contraction for I would, said out loud

explanation.surface: A speaker is amazed by a piece of work in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone open-eyed stares wide in wonder, so the term describes amazement.

clue.text: US patriot always flanked by soldiers

indicators.note: a piece flanked by others has them on both sides, so it sits inside

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British Army soldiers
ever means always

explanation.surface: An American hero is perpetually surrounded by troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Revere was the American Revolutionary hero famed for his midnight ride warning of British troops.

clue.text: Difficult task to find a piece of yellow elastic

parts.note: a stretch is a demanding effort, as in 'that's a bit of a stretch'

indicators.note: a piece of the colour word here means just its opening letter

explanation.surface: It is hard work locating a scrap of yellow rubber band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elastic' looks like a noun for a rubber band, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stretchy can be pulled out and spring back, as a rubber material does.

clue.text: Tasteless articles looking into South American's importance in society

indicators.note: one looking into something pokes inside it, so these letters go within

parts.note: US for American, the 's linking it on
tat is cheap, tasteless goods

explanation.surface: Tacky goods examine a South American's social standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is a person's rank or standing relative to others in a community.
